---
title: "National Parks, Year by Year: Visitation, 2000–2025"
subtitle: "How Park Designation Shapes Annual Attendance Across 9,612 Park-Year Observations"
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
  message: false
---

```{r}
#| label: setup-home
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)

annual_visits <- read_csv(
  "nps_annual_visits_1979_2025.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |>
  filter(year >= 2000, year <= 2025) |>
  mutate(
    suffix = word(park, -1),
    park_type = case_when(
      suffix %in% c("NP", "NPRES", "PRES") ~ "National Parks & Preserves",
      suffix %in% c("NRA", "NS", "NL", "PKWY", "NR", "NSR", "W&SR", "NRRA") ~ "Recreation Areas, Seashores & Parkways",
      suffix %in% c("NM", "Monument") ~ "National Monuments",
      TRUE ~ "Historic Sites, Battlefields & Memorials"
    ),
    park_type = factor(
      park_type,
      levels = c(
        "Recreation Areas, Seashores & Parkways",
        "National Parks & Preserves",
        "Historic Sites, Battlefields & Memorials",
        "National Monuments"
      )
    ),
    y_log = log10(recreation_visits + 1),
    hover_label = paste0(
      "<b>", park, "</b><br>",
      year, " · ", scales::comma(recreation_visits), " visits<br>",
      "<span style='color:#5A6B60;'>", park_type, "</span>"
    )
  )

n_obs <- nrow(annual_visits)
n_parks <- n_distinct(annual_visits$park)
```

## Does Park Designation Shape Annual Crowd Size?

Each dot below is **one National Park Service unit in one calendar year** from **2000 to 2025** (**`r scales::comma(n_obs)` annual observations** across **`r n_parks` units**). Hover over any dot to see which park it represents, explore individual parks on the **[Park Attendance](explore.qmd)** tab, or read the fixed comparison on the **[Visitation After 2020](story.qmd)** tab.

```{r}
#| label: fig-park-visitation-by-type
#| fig-cap: "9,612 annual park-year observations (2000–2025) colored by NPS designation, with solid lines showing each category's yearly median. Hover any dot for park details (drag horizontally to zoom into specific years; double-click to reset). Plotted on a pseudo-log vertical scale so smaller sites remain visible alongside multi-million-visit parks. Source: NPS Visitor Use Statistics."
#| column: body-outset

type_medians <- annual_visits |>
  group_by(year, park_type) |>
  summarize(
    median_visits = median(recreation_visits, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    y_log = log10(median_visits + 1),
    hover_label = paste0(
      "<b>", park_type, "</b><br>",
      year, " category median · ", scales::comma(round(median_visits)), " visits"
    )
  )

palette_cols <- c(
  "Recreation Areas, Seashores & Parkways" = "#4A7C82",
  "National Parks & Preserves" = "#2F6B48",
  "Historic Sites, Battlefields & Memorials" = "#C48347",
  "National Monuments" = "#A45D57"
)

y_breaks <- c(0, 10000, 100000, 1000000, 10000000)
full_x_range <- c(1999.5, 2025.5)
full_y_range <- c(-0.15, log10(24000000 + 1))

p <- plot_ly(height = 530)

for (cat_name in levels(annual_visits$park_type)) {
  cat_pts <- filter(annual_visits, park_type == cat_name)
  cat_med <- filter(type_medians, park_type == cat_name)
  col_hex <- unname(palette_cols[cat_name])

  p <- p |>
    add_trace(
      data = cat_pts,
      x = ~year,
      y = ~y_log,
      type = "scattergl",
      mode = "markers",
      name = cat_name,
      legendgroup = cat_name,
      showlegend = FALSE,
      marker = list(color = col_hex, size = 6.2, opacity = 0.28),
      text = ~hover_label,
      hovertemplate = "%{text}<extra></extra>"
    ) |>
    add_trace(
      data = cat_med,
      x = ~year,
      y = ~y_log,
      type = "scatter",
      mode = "lines",
      name = cat_name,
      legendgroup = cat_name,
      showlegend = TRUE,
      line = list(color = col_hex, width = 2.8),
      text = ~hover_label,
      hovertemplate = "%{text}<extra></extra>"
    )
}

p |>
  layout(
    paper_bgcolor = "#FAF7F0",
    plot_bgcolor = "#FAF7F0",
    hovermode = "closest",
    dragmode = "zoom",
    hoverlabel = list(
      bgcolor = "#FAF7F0",
      bordercolor = "#C8C2B0",
      font = list(family = "system-ui, sans-serif", size = 12.5, color = "#1E382B")
    ),
    margin = list(t = 75, r = 20, b = 45, l = 70),
    legend = list(
      orientation = "h",
      x = 0,
      y = 1.03,
      yanchor = "bottom",
      font = list(size = 12, color = "#223028")
    ),
    xaxis = list(
      title = "",
      range = full_x_range,
      tick0 = 2000,
      tickformat = "d",
      showgrid = FALSE,
      zeroline = FALSE,
      tickfont = list(color = "#4A5B51", size = 12)
    ),
    yaxis = list(
      title = list(text = "Annual visits", font = list(color = "#4A5B51", size = 12.5)),
      range = full_y_range,
      fixedrange = TRUE,
      tickvals = log10(y_breaks + 1),
      ticktext = c("0", "10k", "100k", "1M", "10M"),
      gridcolor = "#E6E1D2",
      zeroline = FALSE,
      tickfont = list(color = "#4A5B51", size = 12)
    )
  ) |>
  config(
    displayModeBar = "hover",
    displaylogo = FALSE,
    scrollZoom = FALSE,
    modeBarButtonsToRemove = c(
      "lasso2d", "select2d", "pan2d", "zoomIn2d", "zoomOut2d", "autoScale2d"
    )
  )
```

## Key Takeaways (2000–2025)

- **Recreation Areas, Seashores & Parkways lead in typical annual crowd size:** Across 1,109 park-year observations (44 units), scenic roadways, seashores, and urban recreation corridors record a median of **1.09 million annual visits**.
- **National Parks & Preserves sustain strong 21st-century attendance:** Across 1,953 park-year observations (76 units), flagship National Parks and Preserves hold a median of **520,171 annual visits**, with top units exceeding 10 million visits per year.
- **Historic Sites & National Monuments form the numerical majority of the system:** Over two-thirds of all 2000–2025 observations (**6,550 of 9,612**) belong to historic sites, battlefields, memorials, and monuments, welcoming medians of roughly **97,000 to 113,000 annual visits**.
